text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Georgi Parvanov is the most likely leader of the Bulgarian Socialist Party while Interior Minister Nikolai Dobrev may become prime minister.

- The deputy chief of parliament's anti-corruption commission Edvin Sugarev said Prime Minister Zhan Videnov's advisors distributed among themselves some $500,000 from each oil shipment to Bulgaria's biggest refinery Neftochim.
- Bulgaria's privatisation agency has received $163 million in proceeds from January 1 to November 30 this year, agency figures show.
- Bulgaria's ambassador in Peru Dimitar Stanoev, one of the hostages held at the Japanese Embassy in Lima, was released.
- Parliament will vote on Prime Minister Zhan Videnov's resignation at an extraordinary session on Saturday. Videnov tendered his resignation at a Socialist party congress last Saturday.

- Forty-six percent of Bulgarian men refuse to have sex at home because of overcrowding caused by more than one generation living in small apartments, showed an opinion poll conducted by ASSA-M agency. Fifty percent of the 1,005 men interviewed are unfaithful, showed the poll.

- Some 70 inefficient state enterprises, isolated from credits since August, have improved their financial results in the second half of this year and have presented their stabilisation programmes, said Finance Minister Dimiter Kostov. The ministry has extended the deadline for the stabilisation programmes until January 22 because most of them needed to be reworked.
- Cigarette prices are expected to rise by 90 percent around the New Year holiday, said the head of tobacco products state monopolist Bulgartabac Evgeni Evgeniev.
- The ambulance service in Sofia is about to stop functioning due to bad debts and antiquated equipment which is too costly to maintain, doctors say.
- Multigroup Bulgaria AD, a powerful local business group, has invested $40 million in Bulgaria, said its president Ilia Pavlov.
